steps.cmd: test -f RULES-OK || { echo 'A person must read the challenge rules at https://huntr.com/challenges and create RULES-OK (one line: automation allowed, rate limit) in funding/orchestrator/work/huntr first'; exit 1; }

steps.prompt: You are preparing an entry for the active huntr AI prompt-injection challenge (listed at https://huntr.com/challenges). Read RULES-OK for the human's notes on what automation and rate limits the rules allow; never exceed them. Using only WebFetch and WebSearch, read the challenge's rules and scoring pages and public write-ups of earlier huntr challenges. Write research.md: target description, scoring, what counts as a valid finding, submission format, allowed and banned techniques, and six distinct attack families to try (role confusion, tool-output injection, encoding tricks, multi-turn trust building, indirect injection via documents, instruction smuggling in structured data). Reply with a 5-line summary.

Read findings/attempts.jsonl and research.md. For every success that replayed twice, draft a submission in SUBMISSION.md in the challenge's required format: title, technique, exact input, observed output, why it meets the rules, reproduction steps. Add a top section 'Human checklist' (huntr account, Stripe Connect KYC, review each finding, submit by hand). Do not submit anything. Reply with the number of findings packaged.
